naming: The loader deserializes with YamlDotNet's CamelCaseNamingConvention and refuses any key it does not know.

keys.description: The platform batch the flow belongs to, which groups flows in listings and batch runs. Part of the platform envelope, which the platform reads itself.
How a change is decided: by the rendered document's hash, by the payload's detection, and what happens to a record found unchanged.

How a document change is decided: `renderedHash` compares the hash of the rendered document with what the ledger holds; `always` delivers every record read. `lastModified` is refused here: the source row's business version column is `source.lastModified`. `contentHash` is refused too: it is how a payload is compared, under `change.payloadDetect`.
What happens to a record whose document and payload are unchanged: `skip` leaves it, `deliver` sends it anyway.

How a payload change is decided: `contentHash` compares the payload's hash column; `lastModified` takes the files as the watermark (a file modified after the delivered ones, or a changed set of files), at one storage listing per record per run; `always` sends the payload every time. `lastModified` is refused on a route that delivers no payload files. `renderedHash` is refused: it is how a document is compared, under `change.detect`.
The tier-0 gate: an incremental run whose window holds no changed row of the record table or its datasets, and no record the ledger asked to plan again, completes without reading a record.
Free text describing the flow. Part of the platform envelope, which the platform reads itself.

When the records' failures add up to a failure of the interface itself (or of the run, for a document without interfaces); a record with a data problem is held and the interface goes on. In a source with interfaces these are every interface's stop rules unless it sets its own.
The interface stops when this many records in a row failed with problems of one class (data, connection or permission), with none delivered in between. At least 1; not set by default.

The interface stops when held and failed records reach this share (above 0, at most 100) of the records the run settled, judged once `minRecords` have settled. A planning pass that holds this share of the records it took up stops the interface before it sends anything. Not set by default.
How many records have to settle before `failedPercent` is judged; at least 1.

The interface stops when this many records in a row could not reach the service (a transport failure, a timeout, HTTP 408, 429 or 5xx) or were refused by it (HTTP 401 or 403), with none delivered in between. 0 turns the rule off.
The document's discriminator: `delivery` for a delivery flow. The loader dispatches on it and refuses a delivery document that names another flow type.

The interfaces of a source: one entry for each OSDU type the source delivers, each with its own record table, mapping, route and ledger, all sharing the document's connection, target and defaults. A document without `interfaces` is the single form, a source with one interface. At most 200 interfaces; an empty map is refused.
keys.appliesWhen: The interface form: `source.record`, `source.datasets`, `source.payloads`, `render.mapping`, `target.protocol`, `target.protocolOptions.payload` and `target.workflow` are then refused at the source level.

keys.description: One interface, named by the key: a letter followed by letters, digits, `_` and `-`, at most 64 characters, unique in the document regardless of case. It declares at least its `record` and its `mapping`; its ledger is kept under `<flow>/<interface>` unless `ledger` names another.

Interfaces of this document this one waits for, beside the ones its records refer to through the mapping's relationships. The loader refuses a name the document does not declare, the interface itself, a name listed twice, and interfaces whose `after:` wait for each other.
The name of another interface of this document that runs before this one.

The DDMS bulk data each record carries: a payload set of the same shape as `files`, written through the record's DDMS after the record. Declaring it takes the interface by the `ddms` route, `fileAndDdms` with `files`, or `manifestAndDdms` with `route: manifest`.
keys.appliesWhen: Refused with `route` storage, dataset, workflow or dspdm, and beside a `workflow` block.

keys.description: An optional record column holding the declared number of files, which spares a listing when planning.

The record column holding the payload's content hash, which decides whether the payload changed. Required for a set the route streams unless `change.payloadDetect` is `lastModified`, where it stays the final check so rewritten files with the same content are not sent again.
The record column holding each record's payload folder, relative to `root` or absolute under it. Required for a set the route streams.
The file name glob the files match under the record's folder (`chunk_*.parquet`). A name only: `/`, `\` and `..` are refused.

The folder or storage prefix the files must sit under, relative to the flow file when it is a relative path. It takes `{parameter}` tokens, whose values must not contain `/`, `\` or `..`; a record whose folder falls outside it is held.
The source's `change` block, with this interface's keys laid over it key by key.

How a document change is decided: `renderedHash` compares the hash of the rendered document with what the ledger holds; `always` delivers every record read. `lastModified` is refused here: the source row's business version column is `source.lastModified`. `contentHash` is refused too: it is how a payload is compared, under `change.payloadDetect`. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
What happens to a record whose document and payload are unchanged: `skip` leaves it, `deliver` sends it anyway. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

How a payload change is decided: `contentHash` compares the payload's hash column; `lastModified` takes the files as the watermark (a file modified after the delivered ones, or a changed set of files), at one storage listing per record per run; `always` sends the payload every time. `lastModified` is refused on a route that delivers no payload files. `renderedHash` is refused: it is how a document is compared, under `change.detect`. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

The tier-0 gate: an incremental run whose window holds no changed row of the record table or its datasets, and no record the ledger asked to plan again, completes without reading a record. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
The interface's child tables, as `source.datasets` declares them.
One child dataset, named by the key: letters, digits and `_`, not starting with a digit, at most 128 characters, and not `record`, which names the record table itself.
How a child row joins its record: child column to record key column. It must cover every key column of the record table, or a child row could belong to several records.
The key is a column of the child table; the value is the record table's key column it joins.
The most child rows one record may carry, 1 to 1000000. A record with more child rows than this is held rather than rendered.
The child table's three-part name, `[database].[schema].[table]`.
The columns child rows are ordered by within a record.
A column of the child table.
Free text describing the interface.
The interface's stop rules, laid over the source's `failWhen` key by key.

The interface stops when this many records in a row failed with problems of one class (data, connection or permission), with none delivered in between. At least 1; not set by default. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

The interface stops when held and failed records reach this share (above 0, at most 100) of the records the run settled, judged once `minRecords` have settled. A planning pass that holds this share of the records it took up stops the interface before it sends anything. Not set by default. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
How many records have to settle before `failedPercent` is judged; at least 1. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

The interface stops when this many records in a row could not reach the service (a transport failure, a timeout, HTTP 408, 429 or 5xx) or were refused by it (HTTP 401 or 403), with none delivered in between. 0 turns the rule off. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

The files each record carries: a payload set (`root`, `locationColumn`, `pattern`, `hashColumn`, `chunkCountColumn`), uploaded and registered before the record, or, on the dataset route, stored and registered as the record. Declaring it takes the interface by the `file` route, or `fileAndDdms` with `bulk`, unless `route` or `workflow` says otherwise.
keys.appliesWhen: Refused with `route` storage or dspdm; required by `route` file and dataset.

keys.description: An optional record column holding the declared number of files, which spares a listing when planning.

The record column holding the payload's content hash, which decides whether the payload changed. Required for a set the route streams unless `change.payloadDetect` is `lastModified`, where it stays the final check so rewritten files with the same content are not sent again.
The record column holding each record's payload folder, relative to `root` or absolute under it. Required for a set the route streams.
The file name glob the files match under the record's folder (`chunk_*.parquet`). A name only: `/`, `\` and `..` are refused.

The folder or storage prefix the files must sit under, relative to the flow file when it is a relative path. It takes `{parameter}` tokens, whose values must not contain `/`, `\` or `..`; a record whose folder falls outside it is held.
The source's `incremental` settings, overridden key by key for this interface.
Seconds one read may run; 0 lets it run as long as the run does, bounded by cancellation. It must not be negative. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

`snapshot`: every result set of a page reads one snapshot, so a record and its child rows always agree. `readCommitted`: each result set reads what is committed when it runs. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

How far below the watermark the next run reads again, 0 to 86400 seconds, so a transaction that committed after the previous read's upper bound is still picked up. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
Record keys per page, 1 to 100000. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

An optional business version column of the interface's record table, overriding `source.lastModified` for this interface. A row later than the version the ledger holds is planned, the same moment is skipped without rendering, and an older one is stale and never sent.

The name of an existing flow whose ledger the interface keeps instead of its own, so consolidating single-kind flows into one source loses no history and sends nothing again that has not changed. Two interfaces of one document never keep the same ledger; at most 200 characters.
The pinned mapping that renders the interface's records, `Name@version`, as `render.mapping` pins it in the single form; a floating reference is refused.
The source's `target.protocolOptions`, with this interface's keys laid over them: a key set here replaces the source's, a map merges key by key, and a list replaces the source's list whole.

Records per write request where the service takes arrays (storage, file, manifest), 1 to 500. The manifest route runs one workflow per batch of up to this many, and the dspdm route saves up to this many rows at once (at most 256). Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
The storage service's bulk soft delete (`POST /records/delete`, up to 500 ids per request), used only for the reversible removal scope. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
The workflow a manifest sent by reference is handed to. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

RAFS: the content schema version of a content table whose file name names none (`nmr.parquet`, not `nmr.1.1.0.parquet`), as `major.minor` or `major.minor.patch`. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
keys.appliesWhen: Routes that reach a DDMS of the rafsV2 shape.

keys.description: The path template of the single-request bulk upload on a DDMS route (`/ddms/v3/welllogs/{id}/data`). Left out, the collection serving the record's entity type supplies it. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

On the manifest route, how long to wait for the search index to list the registered datasets before the manifest names them (0 does not wait). On the file and manifest routes, it also bounds how long a resumed registration waits for the index before registering the file again. It must not be negative. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

The Dataset service path that hands out a storage location (the dataset and workflow routes, and a manifest by reference): a path starting with `/` or an absolute http(s) URL. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

On the file and manifest routes, the kind of the dataset registered per file; on the dataset route, the kind of the dataset a record of another kind refers to. It must be `authority:source:entityType:major.minor.patch`. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
The Dataset service path that registers datasets, up to 20 per request: a path starting with `/` or an absolute http(s) URL. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

The Dataset service path that answers where registered datasets can be read; the dataset route checks it hands out every dataset it registered. A path starting with `/` or an absolute http(s) URL. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

The Dataset service's reversible removal of a dataset record, with `{id}` where the id goes: a path starting with `/` or an absolute http(s) URL. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
The record's `data` property listing its dataset ids, which the file route fills with the registered datasets as `{id}:`. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

Where the Wellbore DDMS is under the endpoint for this interface, a path starting with `/` (`/api/os-wellbore-ddms`). Refused unless the interface is delivered through a DDMS (ddms, fileAndDdms, manifestAndDdms).

The logical, revertible delete, `{id}` being the record id. Default depends on the route (storage: `POST /api/storage/v2/records/{id}:delete`; ddms: the collection's `DELETE .../{id}`). Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
The path that deletes a dataset record and its file when everything is removed (file and manifest routes), `{id}` being the dataset id. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
The path that registers a file's dataset record after the upload (file and manifest routes). Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

The media type a record's files are uploaded as. Left out, `payloadContentType` where the files are the payload, and `application/octet-stream` beside bulk data. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
keys.appliesWhen: Refused on the storage and ddms routes, which upload no files.

keys.description: Where deliver and intake runs ask the legal service to validate the mapping's legal tags (default `/api/legal/v1/legaltags:validate` under the endpoint): a path starting with `/` or an absolute http(s) URL. Needed, as a whole URL, only for a ddms flow whose endpoint is the DDMS itself. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

How a manifest reaches the ingestion workflow: `never`, inline; `always`, stored as a dataset and handed to `byReferenceWorkflowName`; `auto`, by reference for a trigger request above `manifestInlineLimitKb` on a partition that registers that workflow, the batch split into manifests under the limit otherwise. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
keys.appliesWhen: Routes manifest and manifestAndDdms; refused on any other route.

keys.description: With `manifestByReference: auto`, the largest trigger request sent inline, in kilobytes, measured as the request indented by four; 1 to 1048576. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
The manifest's kind, `authority:source:entityType:major.minor.patch`. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
The manifest section every record goes into. Left out, it is derived from each record's kind. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

Wellbore DDMS ceiling: columns per bulk chunk, read from each parquet chunk's footer before anything is sent (500 on targets before OSDU M26). 0 does not check. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

Wellbore DDMS ceiling: cells (rows times columns) per bulk chunk, read from each parquet chunk's footer before anything is sent. 0 does not check. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
Not read for an interface: its route decides which payload set it sends (`files`, `bulk`, or none), and replaces any value written here.
The media type the payload goes as: the bulk data on a ddms route, the files where they are the payload. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

Data keys other systems write (`Datasets`, `DDMSDatasets`, `ExtensionProperties`), read from the stored record and carried into every update. Empty, the rendered document replaces the whole data block. Set here, it replaces the source's list whole for this interface.
A key under the record's `data`.

The path the probe calls to check the target is reachable. Default depends on the route (storage: `/api/storage/v2/info`; ddms: `{root}/about` of every DDMS the flow reaches). Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

The physical purge of the record and every version (storage: `DELETE /api/storage/v2/records/{id}`). On the ddms route a record collection, whose DELETE is logical only, purges here; a DDMS endpoint does not reach storage by a path, so write the whole URL. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

The purge of a record's earlier versions, the latest left live (storage: `/api/storage/v2/records/{id}/versions`). Versions belong to the storage service, so a ddms flow whose endpoint is the DDMS writes the whole URL here. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

The HTTP method of the record write. Default `PUT` on the storage route and `POST` on the Wellbore DDMS; override it with `recordPath` for a facade such as petrodb-api. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

The path that takes the record write. Default depends on the route (storage: `/api/storage/v2/records`; ddms: the collection serving the record's entity type); a path set here is used as written. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
The storage path the manifest route reads the records back from, by id, after a workflow run. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

Where the Register service reads the registration of a DDMS that `target.ddms` names with `register`, with `{id}` where the id goes: a path starting with `/` or an absolute http(s) URL. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
keys.appliesWhen: Refused when no DDMS under `target.ddms` names `register`.

keys.description: Where the file and manifest routes ask the search index while they wait for registered datasets. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

The path template that commits or abandons a bulk session on a DDMS route (`/ddms/v3/welllogs/{id}/sessions/{sessionId}`). Left out, the collection supplies it. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

The path template for one chunk of a bulk session on a DDMS route (`/ddms/v3/welllogs/{id}/sessions/{sessionId}/data`). Left out, the collection supplies it. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
The path template that opens a bulk session on a DDMS route (`/ddms/v3/welllogs/{id}/sessions`). Left out, the collection supplies it. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

`1`: a single chunk goes to the bulk endpoint and more open a session; `0`: always a session. Any other value is refused, since the bulk endpoint replaces the whole bulk on every write. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

Sends `skipdupes=true` on the record write of the storage and file routes. Opt in only once the target is confirmed to compare acl, legal and tags, not just data. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

Extra headers on the signed-URL upload. The Azure blob type (`x-ms-blob-type: BlockBlob`) is added for a `*.blob.core.*` URL anyway. Set here, it is merged key by key over the source's for this interface.
One header of the upload: the key is its name, the value its value.

How long the signed upload URL of the file and manifest routes stays valid, a whole number of minutes, hours or days (`30M`, `12H`, `2D`). Left out, the service's default of one hour. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
The path that hands out a signed landing-zone location (file and manifest routes). Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

Whether deliver and intake runs ask the legal service about the mapping's legal tags first, failing before anything is planned when it refuses one. `false` skips it; storage then refuses a bad tag record by record. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
The batched read a verify pass uses, up to 100 ids per request. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

The path template that reads one record back, for a verify and for the read before an update. Default depends on the route (storage: `/api/storage/v2/records/{id}`). Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
The JSON path in a single-record write's response holding the `id:version` string. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
The `executionContext.Payload.AppKey` of a workflow trigger; it must not be empty. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
The ingestion workflow the manifest route hands its manifests to. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

Where the Workflow service describes a workflow, asked before relying on one; a path starting with `/` or an absolute http(s) URL, containing `{workflow}`. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
Extra `executionContext.Payload` entries of a workflow trigger, beside `AppKey` and `data-partition-id`. Set here, it is merged key by key over the source's for this interface.
One Payload entry: the key is its name, the value its text.
Seconds between two polls of a workflow run's status; at least 1. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
The path that triggers a workflow run, `{workflow}` being the workflow name. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
The path that reports a run's status, `{workflow}` and `{runId}` substituted. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
A workflow run still going after this many minutes fails the try, and the next try resumes polling it; at least 1. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
The interface's record table, as `source.record` declares it: `object`, `key`, `primaryKey` and `scope`.

The record table's key columns, in order: the ingestion flow's `load.keyColumns`, naming the same columns as the mapping's `dataset.key`. The key is what makes one row one deliverable: it derives the record's delivery key and OSDU id and joins the child tables. Each column is named once.
A key column of the record table: 1 to 128 characters, without brackets, control characters or surrounding space.
The record table's three-part name, `[database].[schema].[table]` (`OsduData.arc.WellLog`). A two-part name is refused.

The record table's identity primary key (the ingestion flow's `target.identityColumn`, such as `RecId`): an integer identity column that is the table's single-column primary key. A read pages by it and a fan-out cuts its slices on it; it is required when `reliability.fanOut` is above 0.

Binds record table columns to flow parameters: each entry becomes a typed `[column] = @parameter` predicate, so the value is bound and never substituted into SQL. Every parameter named must be declared under `parameters`.
The key is a column of the record table; the value is the name of the declared parameter whose value that column must equal.
The source's `reliability` block, with this interface's keys laid over it key by key; `parallelInterfaces` is refused here.

Rendered documents per work batch: one file the intake writes, one claim a drain takes, one unit of progress a submission shows. 1 to 100000. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
Records a worker claims from the ledger per round trip. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

How many requests (one record, or one batch of records) a worker has in flight at once, and how many reads a verify pass runs at once. At least 1. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

Member runs a large submission spreads over, 0 to 64; 0 runs everything on the node that claimed the run. It needs the record table's `primaryKey`, whose ranges the members read. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
Below this many records a submission never fans out; at least 1. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
How long a worker's lease on a record lasts before a sweep may reclaim it. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

The target's declared request body ceiling, in bytes; a bigger chunk or file holds the record before anything is sent. 0 means not declared. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
The largest response body a request reads, in bytes. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
Refused here: how many interfaces run at once is the source's own setting. Set it under the top-level `reliability`.
The most requests per second the flow sends; 0 is unlimited. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
Renderers in the intake pipeline on one node, 0 to 256; 0 takes half the machine's processors, at least one. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
Retries: the inline repeats of a request that is safe to repeat, and the record-level backoff across worker passes. Set here, it is laid over the source's block key by key for this interface.

The most tries: a request that is safe to repeat is sent at most this many times inline, and a record whose deliveries fail this many times is marked failed. At least 1. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

How the inline delay between tries of one request grows: `exponential` doubles `baseDelayMs` per try up to `maxDelayMs`; `fixed` waits `baseDelayMs` every time. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
The first inline delay between tries of one request, in milliseconds. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

Whether a service's `Retry-After` is honoured. It is never shortened: a wait within `maxDelayMs` is the floor of the backoff, and a longer one travels with the failure to the record's next attempt. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
The longest inline delay between tries of one request, in milliseconds. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
The backoff before a record's next attempt across worker passes, in minutes, doubling per attempt. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
The longest backoff before a record's next attempt, in minutes. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
HTTP statuses that hold a record instead of retrying it (`[409]`). Set here, it replaces the source's list whole for this interface.
An HTTP status code.
The timeout of one request, in seconds. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

The SSRF allowlist: when it lists hosts, every request, and every redirect hop, must go to one of them. `*.suffix` matches the bare domain and any subdomain. Set here, it replaces the source's list whole for this interface.
A host name, or `*.suffix` for a domain and its subdomains.
Whether TLS certificates are verified. `false` also needs `SQLFLOW_DELIVERY_ALLOW_INSECURE_TLS=true` on the node, or the run is refused. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
What the interface overrides of the source's `render` block: `cacheVersion`, and `parameters` merged over the source's. The mapping is the interface's own `mapping` key.

The version of the target partition's cache the mapping renders with. `current` takes whichever version is current when the run starts and records it in the render context; a version label (`20260908T212727Z`) pins that version, and a run fails before anything renders when the catalog does not hold it. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
Values for the mapping's parameters, merged key by key over the source's `render.parameters` for this interface. They enter the render context, so a changed value renders the records again.
The key is a parameter the mapping declares; the value is a literal or a `${env:NAME}` reference.

Names the route instead of letting what the interface declares decide it. A named route and a part only another route sends make their composition (`file` with `bulk` is `fileAndDdms`, `manifest` with `bulk` is `manifestAndDdms`); a route that cannot deliver what the interface declares is refused.
The source's system columns, merged column by column for this interface; a column the interface opts out of (`fileName: ~`) stays opted out for it.

The soft-delete stamp. A record row the ingestion table marked deleted is held and never delivered; the default is used when the table carries it, a column named here must exist, and `~` opts out. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

The column naming the file a row was landed from, recorded in the ledger as the record's origin (at most 800 characters). `~` opts out of recording the origin file. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
The column holding the row's position in that file, recorded with the origin file in the ledger. `~` opts out. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.

The date and time column the incremental window is taken on and a record's fingerprint is built from. SQLFlow's ingestion stamps it on insert, and on update only when the row's checksum changed. It cannot be opted out of. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
The source's `verify` block, with this interface's keys laid over it.
Whether the verify pass re-queues drifted or missing records for redelivery. Set here, it overrides the source's value for this interface.
The workflow each record starts; declaring it takes the interface by the workflow route.
keys.appliesWhen: Refused beside `bulk`, and with a `route` other than `workflow`.

keys.description: How the record is written first: `dataset`, registered with its `files` through the dataset service, or `storage`. Left out, `dataset` when the record carries files and `storage` otherwise; `dataset` without files is refused.

A tag key (a letter, then letters, digits and `_`, at most 64 characters) the route writes on the record with a value derived from its id (`osdu-delivery-<24 hex>`). Templates read it as `{anchorTag}`.
Payload sets registered through the dataset service as the workflow's inputs, at most 8, in document order: one dataset per file, or one collection, under an id derived from the record's.
One input, named by the key: a letter, then letters, digits, `_` and `-`, at most 32 characters, and not a name another payload set has (`files`, `bulk`). Templates read its ids as `{input:name}`.
An optional record column holding the declared number of files, which spares a listing when planning.
The dataset kind each file is registered as; it must be a dataset kind, `authority:source:dataset--Type:major.minor.patch`.

The record column holding the payload's content hash, which decides whether the payload changed. Required for a set the route streams unless `change.payloadDetect` is `lastModified`, where it stays the final check so rewritten files with the same content are not sent again.
The record column holding each record's payload folder, relative to `root` or absolute under it. Required for a set the route streams.
Whether a record may carry no files for this input; the context then reads an empty list.
The file name glob the files match under the record's folder (`chunk_*.parquet`). A name only: `/`, `\` and `..` are refused.

The folder or storage prefix the files must sit under, relative to the flow file when it is a relative path. It takes `{parameter}` tokens, whose values must not contain `/`, `\` or `..`; a record whose folder falls outside it is held.

How the records the runs wrote are found once the last run finished: one of `anchor`, `ids`, `artefact`, `search`, `manifest` or `xcom`, or none, with `minimum`, `waitSeconds`, `keep` and `remove`. Naming two ways is refused.
True when the run writes the record itself, which is then read back.
Finds the records through the record's `data.Artefacts` entries of a role and kind.
The text the artefact's resource kind contains.
The artefact role (`ConvertedContent`).
A template naming the ids the run writes.
How many of the ids found are kept on the record, 0 to 1000; the count is always kept.
A template naming a manifest dataset; the records are the ones the manifest names, read from its retrieval instructions.

How many records the runs must have written for the delivery to count; fewer fails the try, and the next try looks again without running the workflows again. It must not be negative, and above 0 needs a way to find them.
keys.default: 1 (0 with no way named, or with anchor)

keys.description: Whether a removal of the record takes the records its runs created with it.
Finds the records with a search by cursor.
The kind searched, a template (`*:*:*--*:*.*.*`).
The search query, a template (`data.Tags:"{anchorTag}"`).
How long the results are looked for, asked again every `protocolOptions.workflowPollSeconds` until `minimum` records are present; for a search, how long it waits for the index. 0 to 86400 seconds.
Finds the records' ids in an XCom entry of the last run.
The XCom key under that task.
The entity type the record ids taken from the entry must have (`dataset--File.Generic`); left out, every id.
The Airflow task whose XCom entry holds the ids.
When a delivery starts the runs: `changed`, when it writes the record or an input; `created`, only for a new record; `requested`, only when a redelivery names `workflow`.
Names a context uses as `{secret:name}`, each a `${env:...}` or `${keyvault:...}` reference. Each is resolved only for the trigger request, and every step and message shows `***`.
One secret: the key is a letter followed by letters, digits, `_` and `-`; the value must be a whole `${env:NAME}` or `${keyvault:NAME}` reference, never a credential.
The workflow runs, 1 to 4, run in order; a stage's outputs are what later stages and the results read.
One workflow run: the workflow, its execution context, its timing and its outputs.

The execution context, any YAML, with placeholders in its strings (`{partition}`, `{record:path}`, `{input:name}`, `{stage:n.output}`, `{secret:name}` and others). It is checked against the workflow's contract when the document loads, and filled and checked again before every trigger.
One entry of the execution context: any YAML value the workflow reads, with placeholders in its strings.
The known workflow whose payload contract the context follows, when `workflow` is not one of its names. The Workflow service's test DAG is refused.
Values the run produces, read by later stages and the results as `{stage:n.name}`.
One output, named by the key (a letter, then letters, digits, `_` and `-`, at most 64 characters): a `value` template or an `xcom` entry, exactly one of the two.
A template the value is, known before the run.
The XCom entry of the run the value is read from: through the Workflow service's `latestInfo`, which serves the run's latest task only, or from Airflow's REST API when `target.airflow` is declared.
The XCom key under that task.
The entity type the record ids taken from the entry must have; left out, every id.
The Airflow task whose XCom entry holds the value.
How often the run is polled, 0 to 3600 seconds; 0 or left out takes `protocolOptions.workflowPollSeconds`.
How long the run may take, 0 to 10080 minutes (a week); 0 or left out takes the longer of `protocolOptions.workflowTimeoutMinutes` and the contract's.
The workflow as the partition registers it (letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.`). The run's preflight asks the Workflow service for it.

The flow's name: its pipeline in the catalog, its schedules and its run history; the flow id is derived from it. In the single form the ledger keeps the flow under this name (at most 200 characters); an interface's ledger is kept under `<name>/<interface>`.

The flow's own parameters, supplied by `--set name=value` or by the run's values. `{name}` tokens are substituted in `source.work` and each payload set's `root`, and `source.record.scope` binds a parameter to a record column instead.
One parameter, named by the key and referenced as `{name}`. A value supplied for a name not declared here is refused.
The value used when a run supplies none.
Text describing the parameter.

Whether a run must supply a value when the parameter has no default; without one the run fails validation (`parameter 'name' is required`). A schedule must then give it under `values`, since a fire supplies nothing on its own.
How deliveries run: concurrency, retries, timeouts, the URL guard, leases, batches and fan-out. In a source with interfaces it applies to every interface, each able to lay its own keys over it.
Rendered documents per work batch: one file the intake writes, one claim a drain takes, one unit of progress a submission shows. 1 to 100000.
Records a worker claims from the ledger per round trip.
How many requests (one record, or one batch of records) a worker has in flight at once, and how many reads a verify pass runs at once. At least 1.
Member runs a large submission spreads over, 0 to 64; 0 runs everything on the node that claimed the run. It needs the record table's `primaryKey`, whose ranges the members read.
Below this many records a submission never fans out; at least 1.
How long a worker's lease on a record lasts before a sweep may reclaim it.
The target's declared request body ceiling, in bytes; a bigger chunk or file holds the record before anything is sent. 0 means not declared.
The largest response body a request reads, in bytes.
How many interfaces of one wave run at once, 1 to 32. It is the source's own setting: refused on an interface and in a document that declares no interfaces.
The most requests per second the flow sends; 0 is unlimited.
Renderers in the intake pipeline on one node, 0 to 256; 0 takes half the machine's processors, at least one.
Retries: the inline repeats of a request that is safe to repeat, and the record-level backoff across worker passes.
The most tries: a request that is safe to repeat is sent at most this many times inline, and a record whose deliveries fail this many times is marked failed. At least 1.
How the inline delay between tries of one request grows: `exponential` doubles `baseDelayMs` per try up to `maxDelayMs`; `fixed` waits `baseDelayMs` every time.
The first inline delay between tries of one request, in milliseconds.
Whether a service's `Retry-After` is honoured. It is never shortened: a wait within `maxDelayMs` is the floor of the backoff, and a longer one travels with the failure to the record's next attempt.
The longest inline delay between tries of one request, in milliseconds.
The backoff before a record's next attempt across worker passes, in minutes, doubling per attempt.
The longest backoff before a record's next attempt, in minutes.
HTTP statuses that hold a record instead of retrying it (`[409]`).
An HTTP status code.
The timeout of one request, in seconds.
The SSRF allowlist: when it lists hosts, every request, and every redirect hop, must go to one of them. `*.suffix` matches the bare domain and any subdomain.
A host name, or `*.suffix` for a domain and its subdomains.
Whether TLS certificates are verified. `false` also needs `SQLFLOW_DELIVERY_ALLOW_INSECURE_TLS=true` on the node, or the run is refused.

The only block that changes what a document is: the pinned mapping, the cache version and the mapping's parameters enter the render context, so changing them renders the records again. Everything else changes only how a document gets there.
keys.appliesWhen: Required in the single form. In a source with interfaces it holds the shared `cacheVersion` and `parameters`, and `render.mapping` is refused.

keys.description: Not a setting any more: a flow reads the cache of the partition it delivers to (`target.headers.data-partition-id`). A document that still declares `render.cache` is refused when it loads; remove it.

The version of the target partition's cache the mapping renders with. `current` takes whichever version is current when the run starts and records it in the render context; a version label (`20260908T212727Z`) pins that version, and a run fails before anything renders when the catalog does not hold it.
The mapping that renders each record, pinned as `Name@version` (`WellLog@1.4.0`); a floating reference is refused.
keys.appliesWhen: Required in the single form. Refused when the document declares interfaces: each interface pins `interfaces.<name>.mapping`.

keys.description: The directory the flow's mappings are read from, relative to the flow file. Left out, the nearest `mappings` folder walking up from the flow file is used.

Values for the parameters the mapping declares, as literals or `${env:...}` references. They enter the render context, so a changed value renders the records again; in a source with interfaces an interface's `render.parameters` are merged over these.
The key is a parameter the mapping declares; the value is a literal or a `${env:NAME}` reference.

Where the records come from: the keyed ingestion tables SQLFlow's own pre-ingestion and ingestion flows load, on the database `connection` names. In a source with interfaces it holds what every interface shares: `connection`, `work`, `lastModified`, `systemColumns` and `incremental`.

The ingestion database, resolved on the node that runs the flow: a `${env:NAME}` or `${keyvault:vault/secret}` reference, or a SQL Server connection string without a literal password. A literal password is refused; a flow document holds references only.
Child ingestion tables the mapping repeats, by the name the mapping reads them under, each joined to the record table on the record key.
keys.appliesWhen: Single form. Refused at the source level when the document declares interfaces: each interface declares its own `datasets`.

keys.description: One child dataset, named by the key: letters, digits and `_`, not starting with a digit, at most 128 characters, and not `record`, which names the record table itself.
How a child row joins its record: child column to record key column. It must cover every key column of the record table, or a child row could belong to several records.
The key is a column of the child table; the value is the record table's key column it joins.
The most child rows one record may carry, 1 to 1000000. A record with more child rows than this is held rather than rendered.
The child table's three-part name, `[database].[schema].[table]`.
The columns child rows are ordered by within a record.
A column of the child table.
How a run reads what changed since the last run: how far below the watermark it reads again, the page size, the isolation and the command timeout.
Seconds one read may run; 0 lets it run as long as the run does, bounded by cancellation. It must not be negative.
`snapshot`: every result set of a page reads one snapshot, so a record and its child rows always agree. `readCommitted`: each result set reads what is committed when it runs.
How far below the watermark the next run reads again, 0 to 86400 seconds, so a transaction that committed after the previous read's upper bound is still picked up.
Record keys per page, 1 to 100000.

An optional business version column of the record table: a `datetime`, or text holding RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 (read as UTC without an offset). A row later than the version the ledger holds is planned, the same moment is skipped without rendering, and an older one is stale and never sent; an empty or unreadable value holds the record.

The file sets a streaming route sends, by name. Each record's folder is named by a column of its row, and the files are read where they sit; a route that sends both files and bulk data reads them under the names `files` and `bulk`.
keys.appliesWhen: Single form. Refused at the source level when the document declares interfaces: an interface declares `files` and `bulk` instead.

keys.description: One payload set, named by the key. When several are declared, `target.protocolOptions.payload` names the one the route streams; a set the route would never send is refused.
An optional record column holding the declared number of files, which spares a listing when planning.

The record column holding the payload's content hash, which decides whether the payload changed. Required for a set the route streams unless `change.payloadDetect` is `lastModified`, where it stays the final check so rewritten files with the same content are not sent again.
The record column holding each record's payload folder, relative to `root` or absolute under it. Required for a set the route streams.
The file name glob the files match under the record's folder (`chunk_*.parquet`). A name only: `/`, `\` and `..` are refused.

The folder or storage prefix the files must sit under, relative to the flow file when it is a relative path. It takes `{parameter}` tokens, whose values must not contain `/`, `\` or `..`; a record whose folder falls outside it is held.
The record table, one row per record: its three-part name (`object`), its key columns (`key`), optionally its identity primary key (`primaryKey`) and a `scope` bound to parameters.
keys.appliesWhen: Required in the single form. Refused at the source level when the document declares interfaces: each interface declares its own `record`.

keys.description: The record table's key columns, in order: the ingestion flow's `load.keyColumns`, naming the same columns as the mapping's `dataset.key`. The key is what makes one row one deliverable: it derives the record's delivery key and OSDU id and joins the child tables. Each column is named once.
A key column of the record table: 1 to 128 characters, without brackets, control characters or surrounding space.
The record table's three-part name, `[database].[schema].[table]` (`OsduData.arc.WellLog`). A two-part name is refused.

The record table's identity primary key (the ingestion flow's `target.identityColumn`, such as `RecId`): an integer identity column that is the table's single-column primary key. A read pages by it and a fan-out cuts its slices on it; it is required when `reliability.fanOut` is above 0.

Binds record table columns to flow parameters: each entry becomes a typed `[column] = @parameter` predicate, so the value is bound and never substituted into SQL. Every parameter named must be declared under `parameters`.
The key is a column of the record table; the value is the name of the declared parameter whose value that column must equal.
The names of SQLFlow's system columns on the ingestion tables. A column left out keeps its default; `~` opts out of `fileName`, `rowNumber` or `deleted`.
The soft-delete stamp. A record row the ingestion table marked deleted is held and never delivered; the default is used when the table carries it, a column named here must exist, and `~` opts out.
The column naming the file a row was landed from, recorded in the ledger as the record's origin (at most 800 characters). `~` opts out of recording the origin file.
The column holding the row's position in that file, recorded with the origin file in the ledger. `~` opts out.

The date and time column the incremental window is taken on and a record's fingerprint is built from. SQLFlow's ingestion stamps it on insert, and on update only when the row's checksum changed. It cannot be opted out of.

Where the intake writes its work batches (the rendered documents the drains read back): a directory or storage prefix the nodes can write, relative to the flow file when relative. It takes `{parameter}` tokens, whose values must not contain `/`, `\` or `..`.
Where and how the records are delivered: the endpoint, its credentials and headers, the route and its options. Changing it never redelivers a record by itself.

The Airflow behind the Workflow service, for workflow outputs read from XCom through Airflow's REST API rather than the Workflow service's `latestInfo`, which serves the run's latest task only. Only the workflow route reads it; a flow or interface on another route is refused it.
`v1` (Airflow 2, `/api/v1`) or `v2` (Airflow 3, `/api/v2`). On `v2`, basic credentials are exchanged for a token at `/auth/token`.

How Airflow requests authenticate. Left out, none is sent. Secrets are references only (`${env:NAME}`, `${keyvault:vault/secret}`). On Airflow v2, basic credentials are exchanged for a token at `/auth/token`.
The name of the header an `apiKeyHeader` key is sent in.

The secondary secret: the user name for `basic`, the client id for `oauth2ClientCredentials` (sent as `client_id` unless the token body names one). Always a `${env:NAME}` or `${keyvault:vault/secret}` reference, never a literal.

The primary secret: the token for `bearer`, the key for `apiKeyHeader`, the password for `basic`, the client secret for `oauth2ClientCredentials` (sent as `client_secret` unless the token body names one). Always a `${env:NAME}` or `${keyvault:vault/secret}` reference, never a literal.
keys.appliesWhen: Required when `type` is bearer, apiKeyHeader or basic.

keys.description: The token endpoint an `oauth2ClientCredentials` scheme gets its access token from. The token is reused until shortly before it expires.
The text put before the access token in the `Authorization` header.
Sends the client id and secret as HTTP Basic authentication on the token request instead of in its body.

Form fields of the token request, as literals or references (`scope: ${env:OSDU_SCOPE}`). `grant_type: client_credentials` is added, and `client_id` and `client_secret` from secondarySecretRef and secretRef unless the body names them.
One form field of the token request: the key is the field name, the value a literal or a `${env:...}` / `${keyvault:...}` reference.
An OIDC discovery document URL, literal or a reference; its `token_endpoint` is used as the token URL.
The JSON path of the access token in the token response.
The token endpoint URL, literal or a reference such as `${env:OSDU_TOKEN_URL}`.

The scheme: `none`, `bearer` (secretRef is the token), `apiKeyHeader` (secretRef goes in the header `headerName` names), `basic` (secondarySecretRef is the user, secretRef the password) or `oauth2ClientCredentials` (a client-credentials token from the `token` block).
Text put before the secret in the header: for `bearer` it defaults to `Bearer `, for `apiKeyHeader` to nothing.
The Airflow REST API's base URL: an absolute http(s) URL or a reference to one (`${env:AIRFLOW_URL}`).
Extra headers on every Airflow request.
One header: the key is its name, the value its value or a reference.
How the target's requests authenticate. Left out, none is sent. Secrets are references only (`${env:NAME}`, `${keyvault:vault/secret}`).
The name of the header an `apiKeyHeader` key is sent in.

The secondary secret: the user name for `basic`, the client id for `oauth2ClientCredentials` (sent as `client_id` unless the token body names one). Always a `${env:NAME}` or `${keyvault:vault/secret}` reference, never a literal.

The primary secret: the token for `bearer`, the key for `apiKeyHeader`, the password for `basic`, the client secret for `oauth2ClientCredentials` (sent as `client_secret` unless the token body names one). Always a `${env:NAME}` or `${keyvault:vault/secret}` reference, never a literal.
keys.appliesWhen: Required when `type` is bearer, apiKeyHeader or basic.

keys.description: The token endpoint an `oauth2ClientCredentials` scheme gets its access token from. The token is reused until shortly before it expires.
The text put before the access token in the `Authorization` header.
Sends the client id and secret as HTTP Basic authentication on the token request instead of in its body.

Form fields of the token request, as literals or references (`scope: ${env:OSDU_SCOPE}`). `grant_type: client_credentials` is added, and `client_id` and `client_secret` from secondarySecretRef and secretRef unless the body names them.
One form field of the token request: the key is the field name, the value a literal or a `${env:...}` / `${keyvault:...}` reference.
An OIDC discovery document URL, literal or a reference; its `token_endpoint` is used as the token URL.
The JSON path of the access token in the token response.
The token endpoint URL, literal or a reference such as `${env:OSDU_TOKEN_URL}`.

The scheme: `none`, `bearer` (secretRef is the token), `apiKeyHeader` (secretRef goes in the header `headerName` names), `basic` (secondarySecretRef is the user, secretRef the password) or `oauth2ClientCredentials` (a client-credentials token from the `token` block). The loader refuses bearer, apiKeyHeader and basic without secretRef, apiKeyHeader without headerName, and oauth2ClientCredentials without token.
Text put before the secret in the header: for `bearer` it defaults to `Bearer `, for `apiKeyHeader` to nothing.

The DDMSs the records go to, by names the flow gives them, in document order: a record goes to the one serving its entity type, before the Wellbore DDMS under `protocolOptions.ddmsRoot`. No entity type may be served by two of them, and an empty map is refused.
keys.appliesWhen: Routes ddms, fileAndDdms and manifestAndDdms; refused on any other route in the single form, and in a source where no interface goes through a DDMS.

keys.description: One DDMS, named by the key: a letter followed by letters, digits, `_` and `-`, at most 64 characters, unique regardless of case.
Seismic Store: 0 to 256. On Azure a single file is cut into blobs of this size (0 keeps it one blob); everywhere, the size of each block, piece or part a file goes up in (32 MiB when 0).

The entity types the DDMS serves, each with its collection. Left out, the shape's own collections (the Wellbore DDMS's nine for `wellboreDdmsV3`); an empty map is refused, and the historian takes none.
One served entity type, named with its group (`work-product-component--WellLog`), compared regardless of case.

Whether the collection keeps bulk data beside its records. A Well Delivery DDMS refuses `true`, a Seismic Store refuses `false` (its datasets always keep files), and a Reservoir Management DDMS takes neither, its tables deciding.

What the bulk data's columns are checked against before they are sent: `unchecked`, `curveIds` (every column is a `data.Curves[].CurveID`), `curveIdsAndWidths` (as curveIds, and each curve's `NumberOfColumns`) or `trajectoryStations` (every column is a `data.AvailableTrajectoryStationProperties[].Name`). Only a bulk collection of a Wellbore DDMS takes a check.

The collection's path segment (`welllogs`): letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, at most 100 characters. A Well Delivery DDMS serves each type under the type itself lowercased, a Seismic Store path only names the type, and a Reservoir Management path names one of its nine header collections.
keys.appliesWhen: Required for the wellboreDdmsV3 and rafsV2 shapes, and for a Reservoir Management type that is not one of the service's own.

keys.description: RAFS: the content collection holds several content types, each under its own path segment. Only a bulk collection of the `rafsV2` shape takes it.

Well Delivery DDMS: how many writes one node sends to the deployment at once, 1 to 16. Its Mongo and Cosmos stores keep the collection of the current write in shared state, so writes of different types at once can land in each other's collection.

Seismic Store: the folder under the subproject the datasets are registered in, segments of letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-` (`surveys/north`); leading and trailing slashes are dropped. Left out, the subproject's root.
Production DDMS historian: the largest request body the points are sent in, 10000 to 64000000 bytes. A declared `reliability.maxRequestBodyBytes` below it bounds the requests instead.

Well Delivery DDMS: whether the deployment copies every entity into Storage (`app.entity.storage`), which the API cannot tell. The copy's id is kept on the record, and a removal takes the copy through Storage too.
Seismic Store: the object store's absolute http(s) address, without credentials, query or fragment. Required on `anthos` and `ibm`; on `gc`, another endpoint than `https://storage.googleapis.com`.
Production DDMS historian: the pause between two reads of points the query service does not serve yet. Reservoir Management DDMS: the pause between two asks. 1 to 60 seconds.

The provider the deployment runs on, which the API cannot tell. Well Delivery DDMS: `azure`, `aws`, `gc` or `ibm` (on `ibm` an entity is never written again under a version it already has). Seismic Store: `azure`, `gc`, `anthos` or `ibm`, deciding the object store the files go to; left out, the provider the service names in its `Service-Provider` header.
Production DDMS historian: where its query service is under the endpoint. Each accepted version of the points is read back there, and the probe asks its `/info`.
Seismic Store: whether a delivered dataset is closed read-only. A later delivery of its files lifts the flag, writes, and closes it read-only again.
Seismic Store: the region S3 requests are signed for on `anthos` and `ibm` (lower-case letters, digits and `-`).

The id the DDMS is registered under in the Register service (2 to 50 letters, digits and `-`). What the flow leaves out, its root and its collections, is read from the registration when the flow's protocol is built; refused when the DDMS declares both its root and its collections.

Where the DDMS is under the endpoint, a path starting with `/` (`/api/os-wellbore-ddms`). Left out, the endpoint is the DDMS itself, which only a single-form flow declaring that one DDMS and no `ddmsRoot` can say.
keys.appliesWhen: Required for the productionTimeSeriesV1, seismicStoreV3 and reservoirManagement shapes, and for every DDMS of a source with interfaces unless it names `register`.

keys.description: Production DDMS historian: how long a delivery reads the points it sent back before leaving the record for its next try (0 delivers on the acceptance alone). Reservoir Management DDMS: how long a delivery with rows waits for the service to take its record in (0 asks once). 0 to 3600 seconds.

The DDMS's call pattern: `wellboreDdmsV3` (the Wellbore DDMS v3), `wellDeliveryV1` (the Well Delivery DDMS), `rafsV2` (the Rock and Fluid Sample DDMS), `productionTimeSeriesV1` (the Production DDMS historian), `seismicStoreV3` (Seismic Store v3) or `reservoirManagement` (the Reservoir Management DDMS). The shape decides which other keys the DDMS takes.
Seismic Store: the subproject the datasets are registered in (a lower-case letter, then lower-case letters, digits and `-`). An operator provisions it; the route never creates one.
Seismic Store: the tenant the datasets are registered under (letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`). Left out, the flow's `data-partition-id`, which the tenant equals on OSDU.
The Production DDMS core service (DSPDM) the dspdm route writes business object rows to.
keys.appliesWhen: The dspdm route; refused on any other route in the single form, and in a source where no interface takes the dspdm route.

keys.description: The business objects the flow's kinds are rows of, by the entity type a kind names. A kind not listed is the business object named like its entity.
One entity type, the entity segment of a DSPDM kind (letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.`), such as `well_test`.
The attributes a row is found again by, which must be one of the business object's unique constraints. Left out, its one unique constraint; an empty list is refused.
An attribute name, read in upper case as DSPDM reads it, listed once.
The business object the entity's rows are (`WELL TEST`): at most 50 characters, not starting with a digit, read in upper case. Left out, the entity in upper case with a space for each `_`.

What happens to a row that holds a record's key when the record did not write it: `hold` holds the record and names the row; `update` updates the row and keeps it as the record's, to take over rows loaded before.
Where DSPDM is under the endpoint (`/api/dspdm/v1` behind the GC gateway). Left out when the endpoint is DSPDM itself.

The zone every request names: `GMT+hh:mm` or `GMT-hh:mm`, from GMT-12:00 to GMT+14:00. DSPDM moves a date and time written in the ISO form with an offset into this zone, and keeps any other form as written.

External Data Services: how the records that configure it (connected source registry entries, data jobs and proxy datasets) are checked before they are sent. Without the block they are checked with the defaults.
The eds-dms build the partition runs: `corePlus`, `azure` or `gc`. Only `gc` takes `GcpServiceAccount` schemes; left out, such a scheme is held.
Whether registry entries, data jobs and proxy datasets EDS could not use are held before they are sent. `false` checks nothing, and then `retrieval` and `build` are refused.
Whether registry entries need the `DatasetURL` eds-dms retrieves their datasets through. `false` lets through a registry entry without one.

The base URL requests go to (`${env:OSDU_URL}`); `${env:NAME}` and `${keyvault:vault/secret}` references are resolved on the node. In a source with interfaces it is the platform root every interface reaches its services under; a ddms flow in the single form may point at the DDMS itself.
The Reservoir DDMS the etp route writes Energistics objects to, over ETP 1.2 on a WebSocket.
keys.appliesWhen: The etp route; refused on any other route in the single form. In a source with interfaces it goes to the etp interfaces.

keys.description: The dataspace a record goes into when its document names none: at least three characters of letters, digits and `_ - . /`; two levels (`project/study`) are recommended.
Whether a delivery leaves the dataspace locked, which makes it read-only until the next delivery unlocks it. A locked dataspace refuses every write, including this flow's next one.
The most bytes of one array a delivery reads into memory before it holds the record instead; at least 1024.
The largest message this side offers to send or accept, 64000 to 2000000000 bytes; the session settles on whichever side allows less.
Objects per message, which is also the batch the worker hands the route; 1 to 10000.
Where the ETP WebSocket answers under the endpoint.
Extra headers on every request. It must declare a non-empty `data-partition-id`, which every OSDU service requires; that partition's cache is the one the mapping reads.
One header: the key is its name, the value its value or a `${env:...}` / `${keyvault:...}` reference.

The route the records go by: `storage`, `file`, `dataset`, `manifest`, `ddms`, `fileAndDdms`, `manifestAndDdms`, `workflow`, `dspdm` or `etp`. The names the routes carried before (`osduRecord`, `osduWellLog` and the other `osdu` names) still load.
keys.appliesWhen: Required in the single form. Refused when the document declares interfaces: each interface's route follows from what it declares, or from `interfaces.<name>.route`.

keys.description: The route's settings: service paths, batch sizes, content types and workflow options. Any path option may be written as an absolute URL, guarded like every other request; in a source with interfaces an interface's `protocolOptions` are laid over these.

Records per write request where the service takes arrays (storage, file, manifest), 1 to 500. The manifest route runs one workflow per batch of up to this many, and the dspdm route saves up to this many rows at once (at most 256).
The storage service's bulk soft delete (`POST /records/delete`, up to 500 ids per request), used only for the reversible removal scope.
The workflow a manifest sent by reference is handed to.
RAFS: the content schema version of a content table whose file name names none (`nmr.parquet`, not `nmr.1.1.0.parquet`), as `major.minor` or `major.minor.patch`.
keys.appliesWhen: Routes that reach a DDMS of the rafsV2 shape.

keys.description: The path template of the single-request bulk upload on a DDMS route (`/ddms/v3/welllogs/{id}/data`). Left out, the collection serving the record's entity type supplies it.

On the manifest route, how long to wait for the search index to list the registered datasets before the manifest names them (0 does not wait). On the file and manifest routes, it also bounds how long a resumed registration waits for the index before registering the file again. It must not be negative.
The Dataset service path that hands out a storage location (the dataset and workflow routes, and a manifest by reference): a path starting with `/` or an absolute http(s) URL.

On the file and manifest routes, the kind of the dataset registered per file; on the dataset route, the kind of the dataset a record of another kind refers to. It must be `authority:source:entityType:major.minor.patch`.
The Dataset service path that registers datasets, up to 20 per request: a path starting with `/` or an absolute http(s) URL.
The Dataset service path that answers where registered datasets can be read; the dataset route checks it hands out every dataset it registered. A path starting with `/` or an absolute http(s) URL.
The Dataset service's reversible removal of a dataset record, with `{id}` where the id goes: a path starting with `/` or an absolute http(s) URL.
The record's `data` property listing its dataset ids, which the file route fills with the registered datasets as `{id}:`.

Where the Wellbore DDMS is under the endpoint, a path starting with `/` (`/api/os-wellbore-ddms`); omit it when the endpoint is the DDMS itself. In a source with interfaces it applies to the interfaces delivered through a DDMS.
keys.appliesWhen: Routes ddms, fileAndDdms and manifestAndDdms; refused on any other route in the single form.

keys.description: The logical, revertible delete, `{id}` being the record id. Default depends on the route (storage: `POST /api/storage/v2/records/{id}:delete`; ddms: the collection's `DELETE .../{id}`).
The path that deletes a dataset record and its file when everything is removed (file and manifest routes), `{id}` being the dataset id.
The path that registers a file's dataset record after the upload (file and manifest routes).
The media type a record's files are uploaded as. Left out, `payloadContentType` where the files are the payload, and `application/octet-stream` beside bulk data.
keys.appliesWhen: Refused on the storage and ddms routes, which upload no files.

keys.description: Where deliver and intake runs ask the legal service to validate the mapping's legal tags (default `/api/legal/v1/legaltags:validate` under the endpoint): a path starting with `/` or an absolute http(s) URL. Needed, as a whole URL, only for a ddms flow whose endpoint is the DDMS itself.

How a manifest reaches the ingestion workflow: `never`, inline; `always`, stored as a dataset and handed to `byReferenceWorkflowName`; `auto`, by reference for a trigger request above `manifestInlineLimitKb` on a partition that registers that workflow, the batch split into manifests under the limit otherwise.
keys.appliesWhen: Routes manifest and manifestAndDdms; refused on any other route.

keys.description: With `manifestByReference: auto`, the largest trigger request sent inline, in kilobytes, measured as the request indented by four; 1 to 1048576.
The manifest's kind, `authority:source:entityType:major.minor.patch`.
The manifest section every record goes into. Left out, it is derived from each record's kind.
Wellbore DDMS ceiling: columns per bulk chunk, read from each parquet chunk's footer before anything is sent (500 on targets before OSDU M26). 0 does not check.
Wellbore DDMS ceiling: cells (rows times columns) per bulk chunk, read from each parquet chunk's footer before anything is sent. 0 does not check.
Which `source.payloads` entry the route streams; required when several are declared. Refused on the composed routes, whose parts go by their own names (`files`, `bulk`).
keys.appliesWhen: Single form; refused at the source level when the document declares interfaces.

keys.description: The media type the payload goes as: the bulk data on a ddms route, the files where they are the payload.

Data keys other systems write (`Datasets`, `DDMSDatasets`, `ExtensionProperties`), read from the stored record and carried into every update. Empty, the rendered document replaces the whole data block.
A key under the record's `data`.
The path the probe calls to check the target is reachable. Default depends on the route (storage: `/api/storage/v2/info`; ddms: `{root}/about` of every DDMS the flow reaches).

The physical purge of the record and every version (storage: `DELETE /api/storage/v2/records/{id}`). On the ddms route a record collection, whose DELETE is logical only, purges here; a DDMS endpoint does not reach storage by a path, so write the whole URL.

The purge of a record's earlier versions, the latest left live (storage: `/api/storage/v2/records/{id}/versions`). Versions belong to the storage service, so a ddms flow whose endpoint is the DDMS writes the whole URL here.
The HTTP method of the record write. Default `PUT` on the storage route and `POST` on the Wellbore DDMS; override it with `recordPath` for a facade such as petrodb-api.
The path that takes the record write. Default depends on the route (storage: `/api/storage/v2/records`; ddms: the collection serving the record's entity type); a path set here is used as written.
The storage path the manifest route reads the records back from, by id, after a workflow run.
Where the Register service reads the registration of a DDMS that `target.ddms` names with `register`, with `{id}` where the id goes: a path starting with `/` or an absolute http(s) URL.
keys.appliesWhen: Refused when no DDMS under `target.ddms` names `register`.

keys.description: Where the file and manifest routes ask the search index while they wait for registered datasets.
The path template that commits or abandons a bulk session on a DDMS route (`/ddms/v3/welllogs/{id}/sessions/{sessionId}`). Left out, the collection supplies it.
The path template for one chunk of a bulk session on a DDMS route (`/ddms/v3/welllogs/{id}/sessions/{sessionId}/data`). Left out, the collection supplies it.
The path template that opens a bulk session on a DDMS route (`/ddms/v3/welllogs/{id}/sessions`). Left out, the collection supplies it.
`1`: a single chunk goes to the bulk endpoint and more open a session; `0`: always a session. Any other value is refused, since the bulk endpoint replaces the whole bulk on every write.
Sends `skipdupes=true` on the record write of the storage and file routes. Opt in only once the target is confirmed to compare acl, legal and tags, not just data.
Extra headers on the signed-URL upload. The Azure blob type (`x-ms-blob-type: BlockBlob`) is added for a `*.blob.core.*` URL anyway.
One header of the upload: the key is its name, the value its value.
How long the signed upload URL of the file and manifest routes stays valid, a whole number of minutes, hours or days (`30M`, `12H`, `2D`). Left out, the service's default of one hour.
The path that hands out a signed landing-zone location (file and manifest routes).

Whether deliver and intake runs ask the legal service about the mapping's legal tags first, failing before anything is planned when it refuses one. `false` skips it; storage then refuses a bad tag record by record.
The batched read a verify pass uses, up to 100 ids per request.
The path template that reads one record back, for a verify and for the read before an update. Default depends on the route (storage: `/api/storage/v2/records/{id}`).
The JSON path in a single-record write's response holding the `id:version` string.
The `executionContext.Payload.AppKey` of a workflow trigger; it must not be empty.
The ingestion workflow the manifest route hands its manifests to.
Where the Workflow service describes a workflow, asked before relying on one; a path starting with `/` or an absolute http(s) URL, containing `{workflow}`.
Extra `executionContext.Payload` entries of a workflow trigger, beside `AppKey` and `data-partition-id`.
One Payload entry: the key is its name, the value its text.
Seconds between two polls of a workflow run's status; at least 1.
The path that triggers a workflow run, `{workflow}` being the workflow name.
The path that reports a run's status, `{workflow}` and `{runId}` substituted.
A workflow run still going after this many minutes fails the try, and the next try resumes polling it; at least 1.

What a record's references are checked against before it is sent: `none`, the ledger alone; `storage`, which also asks OSDU's storage service about the ids no record of the ledger holds and holds a record naming one storage does not hold.
keys.appliesWhen: Refused for a single-form flow on the dspdm route, and for a source whose every interface takes the dspdm route.

keys.description: The workflow route's declaration: how the record is written first, the inputs registered, the workflow runs in stages, and how what they wrote is found.
keys.appliesWhen: Single form, with `target.protocol: workflow`, which refuses a document without it. Refused on any other route, and at the source level when the document declares interfaces.

keys.description: How the record is written first: `dataset`, registered with its `files` through the dataset service, or `storage`. Left out, `dataset` when the record carries files and `storage` otherwise; `dataset` without files is refused.

A tag key (a letter, then letters, digits and `_`, at most 64 characters) the route writes on the record with a value derived from its id (`osdu-delivery-<24 hex>`). Templates read it as `{anchorTag}`.
Payload sets registered through the dataset service as the workflow's inputs, at most 8, in document order: one dataset per file, or one collection, under an id derived from the record's.
One input, named by the key: a letter, then letters, digits, `_` and `-`, at most 32 characters, and not a name another payload set has (`files`, `bulk`). Templates read its ids as `{input:name}`.
An optional record column holding the declared number of files, which spares a listing when planning.
The dataset kind each file is registered as; it must be a dataset kind, `authority:source:dataset--Type:major.minor.patch`.

The record column holding the payload's content hash, which decides whether the payload changed. Required for a set the route streams unless `change.payloadDetect` is `lastModified`, where it stays the final check so rewritten files with the same content are not sent again.
The record column holding each record's payload folder, relative to `root` or absolute under it. Required for a set the route streams.
Whether a record may carry no files for this input; the context then reads an empty list.
The file name glob the files match under the record's folder (`chunk_*.parquet`). A name only: `/`, `\` and `..` are refused.

The folder or storage prefix the files must sit under, relative to the flow file when it is a relative path. It takes `{parameter}` tokens, whose values must not contain `/`, `\` or `..`; a record whose folder falls outside it is held.

How the records the runs wrote are found once the last run finished: one of `anchor`, `ids`, `artefact`, `search`, `manifest` or `xcom`, or none, with `minimum`, `waitSeconds`, `keep` and `remove`. Naming two ways is refused.
True when the run writes the record itself, which is then read back.
Finds the records through the record's `data.Artefacts` entries of a role and kind.
The text the artefact's resource kind contains.
The artefact role (`ConvertedContent`).
A template naming the ids the run writes.
How many of the ids found are kept on the record, 0 to 1000; the count is always kept.
A template naming a manifest dataset; the records are the ones the manifest names, read from its retrieval instructions.

How many records the runs must have written for the delivery to count; fewer fails the try, and the next try looks again without running the workflows again. It must not be negative, and above 0 needs a way to find them.
keys.default: 1 (0 with no way named, or with anchor)

keys.description: Whether a removal of the record takes the records its runs created with it.
Finds the records with a search by cursor.
The kind searched, a template (`*:*:*--*:*.*.*`).
The search query, a template (`data.Tags:"{anchorTag}"`).
How long the results are looked for, asked again every `protocolOptions.workflowPollSeconds` until `minimum` records are present; for a search, how long it waits for the index. 0 to 86400 seconds.
Finds the records' ids in an XCom entry of the last run.
The XCom key under that task.
The entity type the record ids taken from the entry must have (`dataset--File.Generic`); left out, every id.
The Airflow task whose XCom entry holds the ids.
When a delivery starts the runs: `changed`, when it writes the record or an input; `created`, only for a new record; `requested`, only when a redelivery names `workflow`.
Names a context uses as `{secret:name}`, each a `${env:...}` or `${keyvault:...}` reference. Each is resolved only for the trigger request, and every step and message shows `***`.
One secret: the key is a letter followed by letters, digits, `_` and `-`; the value must be a whole `${env:NAME}` or `${keyvault:NAME}` reference, never a credential.
The workflow runs, 1 to 4, run in order; a stage's outputs are what later stages and the results read.
One workflow run: the workflow, its execution context, its timing and its outputs.

The execution context, any YAML, with placeholders in its strings (`{partition}`, `{record:path}`, `{input:name}`, `{stage:n.output}`, `{secret:name}` and others). It is checked against the workflow's contract when the document loads, and filled and checked again before every trigger.
One entry of the execution context: any YAML value the workflow reads, with placeholders in its strings.
The known workflow whose payload contract the context follows, when `workflow` is not one of its names. The Workflow service's test DAG is refused.
Values the run produces, read by later stages and the results as `{stage:n.name}`.
One output, named by the key (a letter, then letters, digits, `_` and `-`, at most 64 characters): a `value` template or an `xcom` entry, exactly one of the two.
A template the value is, known before the run.
The XCom entry of the run the value is read from: through the Workflow service's `latestInfo`, which serves the run's latest task only, or from Airflow's REST API when `target.airflow` is declared.
The XCom key under that task.
The entity type the record ids taken from the entry must have; left out, every id.
The Airflow task whose XCom entry holds the value.
How often the run is polled, 0 to 3600 seconds; 0 or left out takes `protocolOptions.workflowPollSeconds`.
How long the run may take, 0 to 10080 minutes (a week); 0 or left out takes the longer of `protocolOptions.workflowTimeoutMinutes` and the contract's.
The workflow as the partition registers it (letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.`). The run's preflight asks the Workflow service for it.
How a verify pass treats what it finds.
Whether the verify pass re-queues drifted or missing records for redelivery.
